title: Bearings and Angles of Elevation and Depression
seo_title: Year 10 Maths: Bearings and Elevation Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Use trigonometric ratios in right-angled triangles to solve problems in two dimensions, including bearings and angles of elevation and depression.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on three-figure bearings and angles of elevation and depression. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, with three figures.
key_sub: Angles of elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal; they are equal.
body_html:
How it works

  • A bearing is measured clockwise from north and written with three figures: 045°, 120°, 300°.
  • The back bearing (A from B) differs by 180° from the bearing of B from A.
  • The angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal; the angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal. They are equal (alternate angles).
  • Draw a right-angled triangle and use tan, sin or cos (SOH CAH TOA). Use the sine or cosine rule if the triangle is not right-angled.
Example

The bearing of B from A is 070°. Find the bearing of A from B.

070° + 180°

Answer: 250°

Example

From 30 m away, the angle of elevation of the top of a tree is 40°. Find its height.

tan 40° = h ÷ 30

h = 30 tan 40°

Answer: 25.2 m

Common mistakes

  • Measuring anticlockwise or from east instead of clockwise from north.
  • Writing 45° instead of the three-figure bearing 045°.
  • Adding 90° instead of 180° for a back bearing.
  • Measuring the angle of depression from the vertical instead of the horizontal.

faq.a: An angle measured clockwise from north, written with three digits, such as 045° or 230°.

faq.q: How do you find a back bearing?
faq.a: Add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°, or subtract 180° if it is more.

faq.q: What is the difference between angles of elevation and depression?
faq.a: Elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal to an object above; depression is measured downwards from the horizontal to an object below. From two points, they are equal.

faq.q: Which trigonometric ratio should I use?
faq.a: Label the sides of the right-angled triangle as opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse from the angle, then choose SOH, CAH or TOA. Height and distance problems usually use tan.

items.q: The bearing of Q from P is 296°. Find the bearing of P from Q.
items.e: The bearing back is 180° different: 296° − 180° = 116°.

items.q: Leo walks on a bearing of 195°, then turns 60° to the left. What is his new bearing?
items.e: Turning right adds to the bearing; turning left subtracts. 195° − 60° = 135°.
